Hi Daniel / Priya —

Quick answers to the items Daniel raised. Happy to expand any bullet into more detail or set up a security call.

1) SOC 2 / HIPAA
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (security & availability) most recently in Q1 2026. We can share the auditor’s letter under an NDA; I’ll coordinate with our security team to provide the report or SOC summary.
- HIPAA: Redwood supports HIPAA customers through our Private deployment and Dedicated offerings. For hosted customers, we offer contractual controls and can sign a BAA in scenarios with PHI — we’ll engage legal early if Amaya expects PHI to flow through the hosted API.

2) Deletion SLAs (primary data vs backups) — high level
- Primary customer data (prompts/responses, user-provided content): default retention for hosted customers is 30 days from ingestion; customers can configure shorter retention on Dedicated/Private.
- Deletion SLA: once a customer requests deletion (API or contractually), we initiate removal from primary stores within 24 hours. Full purge from all online replicas typically completes within 7 days.
- Backups & snapshots: backups are retained on a separate lifecycle. Standard backup retention is 90 days; when a deletion request is initiated, we mark corresponding backup objects for expedited deletion. Expedited purge from backups depends on the backup provider and can take up to 90 days for full cryptographic erasure; we maintain chain-of-custody logs for audit during that process.

3) Log retention
- API request/response logs: default 180 days for hosted customers; can be extended to 365+ as part of enterprise contracts.
- Access/auth logs: default 365 days.
- KV/cache traces are ephemeral by default (not persisted long-term) unless configured for debugging/persistent audit.

4) Encryption & key management
- Data at rest: AES-256.
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 supported).
- Dedicated/Private: option to use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) — we can include key rotation details in a follow-up.

Attachments referenced: Data-Retention-SLA-2026.pdf (attached) and Redwood_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx — both contain tables with exact windows and contract language.

Next step: Marissa — suggest we send the questionnaire link and a short note to procurement. Security is available for a call next week if they want a deeper walkthrough.

Thanks,
